statute_title: Driving Under the Influence of Alcohol, Controlled Substances, or Drugs
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle in West Virginia
While under the influence of alcohol, controlled substances, or drugs
Or had a BAC of .08 or higher
Or was under the combined influence of alcohol and any controlled substance or drug
enhancements: BAC .15 or higher (enhanced penalties and mandatory treatment)
Child under 16 in vehicle (additional penalties under § 17C-5-2(o))
Causing serious bodily injury while DUI (§ 17C-5-4)
notes: Implied consent under § 17C-5-4. Admin license revocation 15 days. Ignition interlock required for repeat offenders. Test refusal results in 1-year revocation.

elements: Defendant drove a vehicle in West Virginia
While under the influence of alcohol or drugs
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment of driving ability
No prior DUI convictions within 10 years
mandatory_minimum: 24 hours imprisonment; license revocation 15 days (may apply for conditional); completion of Safety and Treatment Program
notes: First offense with BAC under .15 may qualify for deferred adjudication. Must complete DUI Safety and Treatment Program. License revocation 15 days minimum.

elements: Defendant drove a vehicle in West Virginia
While under the influence of alcohol or drugs
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment of driving ability
One or more prior DUI convictions within 10 years
notes: Second offense: license revocation 10 years. Third offense: lifetime revocation (eligible for reinstatement after 10 years). Ignition interlock required.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle in West Virginia
While under the influence of any controlled substance
Or under the combined influence of alcohol and any controlled substance or drug
To a degree which renders the defendant incapable of safely driving
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
notes: No per se limit for drugs. Prosecution must show actual impairment. Drug Recognition Experts (DRE) used for evaluation. Includes prescription medications.

elements: Defendant drove a vehicle on a public highway
In willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
notes: Common plea-down from DUI. 6-point license penalty. May result in license suspension.

statute_title: Duty to Stop at Scene of Accident Involving Injury or Death
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to stop at the scene
Defendant failed to provide identification and render assistance
notes: Failure to stop at an accident involving injury or death is a felony. Property damage only is a misdemeanor under § 17C-4-2.

elements: Defendant drove a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or drugs
Defendant's impaired driving proximately caused the death of another person
notes: West Virginia treats DUI-related deaths as an enhanced DUI offense rather than a separate vehicular homicide statute. Mandatory minimum 3 years.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Through criminal negligence while operating a motor vehicle
Without malice
notes: Vehicular deaths without DUI may be charged as involuntary manslaughter. If DUI involved, prosecution typically uses § 17C-5-4 for enhanced penalties.

statute_title: Driving While License Suspended or Revoked
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle on a public road
Defendant's license was suspended or revoked
Defendant had knowledge of the suspension or revocation
notes: Driving on a DUI-related suspension carries enhanced penalties. Conviction extends suspension period.

statute_title: Fleeing from a Law Enforcement Officer in a Vehicle
elements: A law enforcement officer gave a visual or audible signal to stop
Defendant was operating a motor vehicle
Defendant willfully failed to stop
Defendant attempted to flee or elude the officer
notes: Fleeing on foot is a separate misdemeanor. Vehicular fleeing with reckless driving or injury is a felony.

statute_title: Simple Possession of a Controlled Substance
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed a controlled substance
Without a valid prescription
Substance is listed in Schedules I through V
notes: First offense may be eligible for conditional discharge. Upon successful completion of probation, charges dismissed. Drug court diversion available.

elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed marijuana
Without a valid medical cannabis card
Any amount of marijuana for recreational use
notes: Medical cannabis legal under § 16A-12-1 et seq. since 2017 with registered patient card. Recreational marijuana remains illegal. First offense eligible for conditional discharge.

elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed cocaine
Cocaine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Without a valid prescription
notes: Simple possession of cocaine is a misdemeanor. Possession with intent to deliver is a felony under § 60A-4-401(a).

elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Without a valid prescription
notes: Manufacturing methamphetamine is a separate felony under § 60A-4-411 with 2-10 years imprisonment.

statute_title: Manufacture, Delivery, or Possession with Intent — Schedule I or II Narcotic
elements: Defendant manufactured, delivered, or possessed with intent to deliver
A narcotic drug classified in Schedule I or II
Including heroin, cocaine, fentanyl, or oxycodone
notes: Trafficking penalties are significantly enhanced for repeat offenders. Fentanyl trafficking carries additional scrutiny. School zone enhancement doubles penalties.

statute_title: Manufacture, Delivery, or Possession with Intent — Non-Narcotic
penalty_max: 5 years (Schedule I-II non-narcotic); 3 years (Schedule III); 2 years (Schedule IV); 1 year (Schedule V)
elements: Defendant manufactured, delivered, or possessed with intent to deliver
A non-narcotic controlled substance
From Schedule I through V
notes: Non-narcotic Schedule I-II includes hallucinogens, amphetamines. Schedule V delivery is a misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant manufactured or attempted to manufacture a controlled substance
Through chemical synthesis or extraction
Operated a clandestine drug laboratory
notes: Separate from general manufacturing under § 60A-4-401. Clandestine lab statute carries additional cleanup and restitution costs.

elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia with knowledge of its intended use
Paraphernalia used or intended for use in manufacturing, growing, or consuming a controlled substance
enhancements: Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor (felony — 1-5 years)
notes: Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor under 18 is a felony. Needle exchange programs authorized under public health statutes.

penalty_min: 1 year (Schedule I-II narcotic); lesser for other schedules
penalty_max: 15 years (Schedule I-II narcotic); 5 years (Schedule I-II non-narcotic)
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
With intent to manufacture or deliver
Intent inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, cash, communications
notes: Intent may be inferred from circumstantial evidence. Quantity thresholds, packaging, and presence of distribution materials are key factors.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
With malice aforethought
With premeditation and deliberation
Or by lying in wait, or by poison, or during commission of arson, robbery, sexual assault, kidnapping, or burglary
mandatory_minimum: Life with mercy recommendation (15 years before parole eligibility); life without mercy (no parole)
notes: West Virginia abolished the death penalty in 1965. Jury recommends mercy or no mercy. With mercy: eligible for parole after 15 years. Without mercy: no parole.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
With malice aforethought
Without premeditation or deliberation
notes: Second degree murder requires malice but not premeditation. Includes depraved heart murder — extreme recklessness showing indifference to human life.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Without malice
Upon sudden quarrel or in the heat of passion
Or upon provocation
notes: Provocation must be such as would cause a reasonable person to lose self-control. Cooling-off period negates heat-of-passion defense.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Through criminal negligence
Or during commission of an unlawful act not amounting to a felony
notes: Involuntary manslaughter may be charged as a misdemeanor or felony depending on the circumstances. DUI-related deaths typically charged under § 17C-5-4.

statute_title: Malicious Assault (Wounding with Intent to Maim, Disfigure, Disable, or Kill)
elements: Defendant maliciously shot, stabbed, cut, or wounded another person
Or caused bodily injury by means of any weapon or substance
With intent to maim, disfigure, disable, or kill
enhancements: Victim is a law enforcement officer
notes: West Virginia distinguishes between malicious assault (intent to maim/kill) and unlawful assault (no specific intent). Malicious assault is the aggravated form.

elements: Defendant unlawfully and intentionally made physical contact
With another person of an insulting or provoking nature
Or caused physical harm to another person
notes: Simple battery in West Virginia is a misdemeanor. Assault (threat without contact) is also a misdemeanor. Battery requires physical contact.

statute_title: Unlawful Assault (Wounding Without Intent to Kill)
elements: Defendant unlawfully shot, stabbed, cut, or wounded another person
Or assaulted or beat another person causing bodily injury
Without intent to kill or maim
notes: Unlawful assault is the mid-tier assault in West Virginia — between simple battery (misdemeanor) and malicious assault (felony with intent to maim/kill).

elements: Defendant took property from the person or in the presence of another
By violence or threat of violence
Against the will of the victim
notes: West Virginia has a single robbery statute. Armed robbery is charged as robbery with additional weapons charges.

statute_title: Robbery with Firearm or Deadly Weapon
elements: Defendant committed robbery
While armed with a firearm or deadly weapon
Or displayed what appeared to be a firearm or deadly weapon
mandatory_minimum: 10 years (robbery); additional consecutive sentence for firearm
enhancements: Use of firearm (5-year consecutive enhancement under § 61-7-11a)
notes: Armed robbery is charged as robbery plus a firearm enhancement. The firearm enhancement runs consecutive to the robbery sentence.

elements: Defendant unlawfully seized, confined, or detained another person
And transported that person from one place to another
Against their will
By force, threat, or deception
mandatory_minimum: 20 years (if victim released unharmed); life (if victim physically injured or not released)
notes: West Virginia kidnapping carries severe mandatory minimums. No parole eligibility for life sentence without mercy recommendation.

elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously set fire to or burned
A dwelling house or outbuilding
Whether owned by defendant or another
enhancements: Death results (first degree murder charge possible)
notes: Second degree arson (§ 61-3-2) covers non-dwelling structures — 1-10 years. Third degree (§ 61-3-3) covers personal property — 1-3 years.

elements: Defendant took a direct act toward committing murder
With specific intent to kill
Act went beyond mere preparation
notes: Attempted felonies in West Virginia are punished under the general attempt statute. Maximum is typically the minimum sentence for the completed offense.

elements: Defendant maliciously assaulted another person
Using a deadly weapon
With intent to maim, disfigure, disable, or kill
notes: Malicious assault with a weapon is the most serious assault charge. Without specific intent, it may be charged as unlawful assault under § 61-2-9(b).

elements: Defendant took and carried away the personal property of another
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
Value of property $1,000 or more
notes: Grand larceny threshold is $1,000. Values below $1,000 are petit larceny (misdemeanor).

elements: Defendant took and carried away the personal property of another
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
Value of property $1,000 or more
notes: West Virginia uses 'grand larceny' for theft of property valued at $1,000 or more.

elements: Defendant took and carried away the personal property of another
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
Value of property less than $1,000
enhancements: Third offense becomes a felony (1-5 years)
notes: Third petit larceny conviction is a felony. Shoplifting also prosecuted under this statute.

elements: Defendant willfully concealed unpurchased merchandise of a store
Or altered a price tag or label
Or transferred merchandise between containers
With intent to deprive the merchant
notes: West Virginia has a specific shoplifting statute. Retailers may also pursue civil recovery up to $750 plus retail value.

statute_title: Entry of Building Other Than Dwelling — Burglary
elements: Defendant broke and entered
A non-dwelling building or structure
With intent to commit a crime therein
notes: Daytime dwelling burglary is covered under § 61-3-11(a). Nighttime dwelling burglary (§ 61-3-11(a)) carries 1-15 years.

elements: Defendant broke and entered
A dwelling house or building adjoining and occupied as a dwelling
With intent to commit a crime therein
notes: Nighttime residential burglary traditionally carries higher sentences. Armed burglary of a dwelling may be charged alongside robbery.

statute_title: Grand Larceny of a Motor Vehicle / Unauthorized Taking
elements: Defendant took a motor vehicle belonging to another
Without consent of the owner
With intent to permanently deprive (larceny) or temporarily use (unauthorized taking)
notes: Joyriding (unauthorized temporary use) is charged under § 17A-8-4 as a felony with up to 5 years. Permanent theft is grand larceny.

elements: Defendant received, concealed, or transferred stolen property
Knowing or having reason to believe the property was stolen
notes: Penalty mirrors the value thresholds of the underlying theft — $1,000 divides felony from misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant unlawfully and intentionally destroyed or damaged property of another
Without the owner's consent
notes: Felony threshold is $2,500 in damages. Restitution typically ordered in addition to criminal penalties.

elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained on property of another
Without permission or lawful authority
After being notified to leave or seeing no-trespassing signs
notes: Trespass on critical infrastructure (pipelines, utilities, mines) is a separate felony. Posted land with purple paint markers creates constructive notice.

statute_title: Destruction or Injury to Property (Criminal Mischief)
elements: Defendant intentionally or recklessly damaged property of another
Without the owner's consent
notes: West Virginia uses 'destruction of property' rather than 'criminal mischief.' Same statute covers both vandalism and reckless damage.

elements: Defendant unlawfully and intentionally made physical contact
Of an insulting or provoking nature with a family or household member
Or caused physical harm to a family or household member
enhancements: Second offense within 10 years (24-hour mandatory minimum)
notes: Family/household member includes spouse, former spouse, persons with a child in common, cohabitants, or persons in a dating relationship. Protective orders under § 48-27-501.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); Felony (third+ or causing serious injury)
elements: Defendant intentionally made physical contact of an insulting or provoking nature
With a family or household member
Or caused physical harm to a family or household member
notes: Domestic assault (§ 61-2-9d) covers threatening a family member — misdemeanor (first/second); felony (third+). Federal firearms prohibition applies to misdemeanor DV convictions.

statute_title: Child Neglect Creating Risk of Injury
elements: Defendant was a parent, guardian, or custodian of a minor child
Defendant's negligent treatment created a substantial risk of bodily injury
Or resulted in bodily injury to the child
notes: Child neglect resulting in death carries 3-15 years. Child abuse causing bodily injury (§ 61-8D-3) carries 1-5 years.

elements: Defendant was a parent, guardian, or custodian of a child
Defendant knowingly or intentionally inflicted physical injury upon the child
Or caused cruel or inhuman treatment
notes: Child abuse causing death (§ 61-8D-2) carries 3-15 years. Pattern of abuse treated more severely.

elements: A valid domestic violence protective order was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant violated the terms of the order
notes: Mandatory minimum confinement for every violation. Third violation within a 10-year period is a felony.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); Felony (second+ or violation of protective order)
elements: Defendant knowingly and willfully engaged in a pattern of conduct
Reasonably calculated to intimidate, harass, or place the victim in fear
Of bodily injury or death
notes: Pattern of conduct requires two or more acts. Cyberstalking included. Second offense or stalking in violation of a protective order is a felony.

elements: Defendant knowingly made repeated unwanted contact with another person
Or communicated threats to another person
At a time or in a manner that would cause a reasonable person to feel harassed
notes: Harassment is a lesser included offense of stalking. Includes telephone harassment and electronic communications.

statute_title: Abuse or Neglect of an Incapacitated Adult
elements: Defendant was a caretaker or person with a duty of care
Victim was an incapacitated adult or elder
Defendant knowingly or intentionally abused or neglected the victim
notes: Financial exploitation of an elder is a separate felony under § 61-2-29b. Adult Protective Services must be notified.

statute_title: Unlawful Possession of Firearms by Prohibited Persons
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant was a prohibited person (convicted felon, involuntarily committed, subject to DV protective order, etc.)
enhancements: Possession during commission of another crime
notes: West Virginia is a constitutional carry state (no permit required for concealed carry) but prohibited persons remain barred. Prohibitions include felony convictions and certain DV misdemeanors.

statute_title: Possession of a Firearm by a Convicted Felon
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant had previously been convicted of a felony
Including felonies involving violence, narcotics, or crimes against persons
enhancements: Possession during commission of another felony (additional consecutive enhancement under § 61-7-11a)
notes: Federal felon-in-possession (18 U.S.C. § 922(g)) may also apply. West Virginia does not have a restoration-of-rights process for firearm possession after felony conviction.

statute_title: Carrying a Deadly Weapon Without License — Prohibited Persons
elements: Defendant carried a concealed deadly weapon
Defendant was a prohibited person or under 21 without a permit
notes: West Virginia enacted constitutional carry in 2016 for persons 21+ who are not prohibited. Persons 18-20 need a provisional license. Under 18 is unlawful.

elements: Defendant discharged a firearm
In a manner that created substantial risk of death or serious bodily harm to another person
enhancements: In a residential area or public place
notes: Separate from brandishing (§ 61-7-11). Discharging a firearm in a public place or near a dwelling is prosecuted under this statute.

statute_title: Taking Identity of Another Person; Penalty
elements: Defendant knowingly took the personal identification of another person
Including name, Social Security number, or financial account information
With intent to fraudulently represent themselves as the other person
notes: Includes use of identification information to obtain credit, goods, or services. Restitution to victims is standard.

elements: Defendant was entrusted with personal property of another
Defendant fraudulently converted the property to own use
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: West Virginia has a specific embezzlement statute. Public officer embezzlement carries enhanced penalties. Threshold is $1,000 for felony.

elements: Defendant falsely made, altered, forged, or counterfeited a writing
With intent to defraud
Writing includes checks, deeds, contracts, public records
enhancements: Uttering a forged instrument (§ 61-4-6 — same penalties)
notes: Uttering (passing a forged instrument knowing it is forged) is a separate offense with the same penalties.

elements: Defendant knowingly devised or participated in a scheme to defraud
Through false representations, promises, or pretenses
To obtain money, property, or services
notes: Covers wire fraud, mail fraud, and other scheme-based fraud. Restitution required.

elements: Defendant used a credit card, debit card, or account number
Obtained without consent of the cardholder
With intent to defraud
notes: Includes stolen, forged, or expired credit card use. Aggregation of multiple transactions allowed for felony threshold.

fine_max: $500,000 or twice the value of the transaction
elements: Defendant conducted a financial transaction
Involving proceeds known to be derived from criminal activity
With intent to promote or conceal the criminal activity
notes: West Virginia Money Laundering Act covers structuring, layering, and integration of criminal proceeds.

statute_title: Sexual Assault in the First Degree
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual intercourse or sexual intrusion with another person
By forcible compulsion
And inflicted serious bodily injury
Or used a deadly weapon
notes: Sexual assault 2 (§ 61-8B-4) is 10-25 years for forcible compulsion without serious injury or weapon. Sexual assault 3 (§ 61-8B-5) is 1-5 years.

statute_title: Sexual Assault in the First Degree
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual intercourse with another person
By forcible compulsion
And inflicted serious bodily injury or used a deadly weapon
notes: West Virginia uses 'sexual assault' rather than 'rape.' First degree sexual assault with a child under 12 carries 25-100 years.

elements: Defendant intentionally exposed private parts
In a public place or in view of the public
Under circumstances likely to cause affront or alarm
enhancements: In the presence of a minor
notes: Exposure to a minor may be prosecuted as sexual abuse under § 61-8D-5. Repeat offenses may trigger sex offender registration.

elements: Defendant offered or agreed to pay a fee
For the purpose of engaging in sexual conduct
notes: Promoting prostitution is a felony. Soliciting a minor for prostitution triggers human trafficking charges.

statute_title: Use of Minors in Filming Sexually Explicit Conduct
elements: Defendant caused or knowingly permitted a minor to engage in sexually explicit conduct
For the purpose of producing a visual portrayal
notes: Possession of child pornography (§ 61-8C-3) is also a felony — up to 5 years. Distribution carries enhanced penalties.

statute_title: Failure to Register as a Sex Offender
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender
Defendant knowingly failed to register, verify, or update registration
notes: Registration required under the Sex Offender Registration Act. Must register within 10 business days of change of address or release.

statute_title: Sexual Assault in the Third Degree (Statutory)
elements: Defendant, aged 16 or older, engaged in sexual intercourse
With a person under 16 years of age
And the age difference was 4 years or more
enhancements: Victim under 12 (first degree sexual assault — 25-100 years)
notes: West Virginia's age of consent is 16. Sexual contact with a child under 12 is first degree sexual assault regardless of force.

elements: Defendant disturbed the peace of others by violent, profane, indecent, or boisterous conduct
Or made unreasonable noise in a public place
notes: General catch-all for public disturbances. Separate from breach of peace statutes.

elements: A law enforcement officer was making a lawful arrest
Defendant knowingly and willfully obstructed or resisted the officer
By use or threat of force or violence
enhancements: Causing physical injury to the officer (felony under § 61-2-10b)
notes: Resisting without force is still a misdemeanor. Assault on an officer during arrest may be charged as a felony separately.

elements: Defendant knowingly and willfully obstructed, delayed, or hindered
A law enforcement officer or judicial officer
In the performance of official duties
notes: Includes providing false information to police, tampering with evidence, and witness intimidation. Witness tampering is a separate felony.

elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a lawful court order
Or engaged in disruptive conduct in court
notes: Summary contempt (in the court's presence) may be punished immediately. Constructive contempt requires notice and hearing.

elements: Defendant appeared in a public place
While visibly intoxicated
And was creating a disturbance or endangering self or others
notes: Law enforcement may take intoxicated persons to a treatment facility instead of jail. Separate from drunk in public disorderly conduct.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (if underlying is misdemeanor); Felony (if underlying is felony)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or personal recognizance
Defendant willfully failed to appear as required by the court
notes: Bail jumping severity matches the underlying charge. Bail bond may be forfeited. Bench warrant issued for arrest.

statute_title: Making a False Report to Law Enforcement
elements: Defendant knowingly made a false statement or report
To any law enforcement officer
Regarding the commission of a crime
notes: Includes filing false police reports. Making a bomb threat or false emergency report carries enhanced penalties.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (general threat); Felony (threat involving WMD or public panic)
elements: Defendant threatened to commit a crime of violence
With intent to terrorize another person
Or with reckless disregard of the risk of causing terror
notes: Bomb threats and hoax WMD threats are separate felonies. Threats causing public panic carry enhanced penalties.

elements: Defendant made a false statement
Under oath in a judicial proceeding or official matter
Knowing the statement was false
The false statement was material
notes: Subornation of perjury (inducing another to commit perjury) carries the same penalties. False swearing in non-judicial proceedings is also punishable.

elements: Defendant offered, gave, or promised something of value
To a public official or public servant
With intent to influence the official's action or decision
notes: Accepting a bribe is also a felony under the same statute. Includes bribery of witnesses and jurors.

elements: Defendant was lawfully confined or in lawful custody
Defendant escaped from confinement or custody
enhancements: Escape from state prison vs. county jail
notes: Sentence for escape runs consecutive to the original sentence. Failure to return from furlough or work release is also escape.

elements: Defendant intentionally tortured, mutilated, or killed an animal
Or cruelly beat or inflicted unnecessary suffering on an animal
notes: Animal fighting is a separate felony. Aggravated animal cruelty involving torture or sadistic conduct is a felony.

offense_class: Varies — court may revoke probation and impose original sentence
elements: Defendant was placed on probation
Defendant violated a condition of probation
notes: Court has discretion to continue, modify, or revoke probation. New criminal charges typically result in revocation. Graduated sanctions available.

offense_class: Varies — return to prison for remaining term
elements: Defendant was released on parole
Defendant violated a condition of parole
notes: Parole Board may revoke parole for any violation. Technical violations may result in graduated sanctions before revocation.

statute_title: Aiding and Abetting — Accessory Before the Fact
elements: Defendant counseled, hired, or procured another to commit a felony
Or aided, abetted, or assisted in the commission of a crime
notes: Accessories before the fact are punished as principals. Accessories after the fact (§ 61-11-7) face lesser penalties.

offense_class: Lesser penalty than completed offense — generally half the maximum
penalty_max: Generally half the penalty for the completed offense
fine_max: Generally half the fine for the completed offense
elements: Defendant had intent to commit a specific crime
Defendant performed an overt act toward committing the crime
Defendant failed to complete the crime
notes: Attempt carries up to half the penalty for the completed offense. Attempt to commit a misdemeanor is also a misdemeanor.

offense_class: Felony (conspiracy to commit felony); Misdemeanor (conspiracy to commit misdemeanor)
penalty_max: 5 years (conspiracy to commit felony); 1 year (conspiracy to commit misdemeanor)
elements: Two or more persons agreed to commit a crime
An overt act was performed in furtherance of the conspiracy
notes: Conspiracy is a separate crime from the underlying offense. Co-conspirators are liable for all acts committed in furtherance of the conspiracy.
